### Historical audit — S0196

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/service_incident_01/retired/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/test/commons_163096530/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines and character ranges in this file.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 1, [0,5609) | The assigned goal was to reconstruct a 512 × 341 indoor photograph as separate SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching camera, framing, placement and materials. This is the requested goal, not evidence that those properties were achieved. The image is referenced by path but is not visible in the supplied observations. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 2, [0,2614) | A fresh, read-only session was launched with the image; it failed with exit code 1 after about 20 seconds. The record reports zero tool calls and no observable model-turn count. |
| Student `model_error`, line 3, [0,537); `scene_error`, line 4, [0,1601) | The failure propagated from the student call through the scene harness. The error points to a stderr log, but its contents are not supplied; the underlying cause is unknown. |

**Outcome:** Technical interruption. No student program, scene change, execution, render, visual inspection, or final submission is visible. This is not evidence of an algorithmic reconstruction failure or an empty patch; correctness remains unknown. No autonomous exploration is recorded.

**Scene-specific checks:** Multiple objects and separate meshes were required, but their creation is unobserved. Materials or textures, connections between parts, pose, camera, lighting, and render quality likewise cannot be assessed. Neither the source photograph nor a generated image is available here for independent visual or geometric verification.

**Teacher and lessons:** No teacher input, detection, diagnosis, proposed update, execution, or adoption appears in this student trajectory. A general operational lesson is that a failed model call can interrupt the scene pipeline before validation; the task-specific scene and failure cause remain unresolved. The referenced stderr log might explain the exit, but that is an untested hypothesis, not an observed diagnosis.
